desk.usage: The cream sheet everything is laid on: the page background, lit from the centre. Ground for ink.

desk-2.usage: The sheet's darker rim, where the radial vignette behind desk ends.

sheet.usage: Plain paper: session rows, search fields, filters, step lists, paper buttons. Ground for ink and mute.

sheet-warm.usage: The chat sheet: the big paper behind the tab row and the thread.

card.usage: The whitest paper: the leaf laid over the tabs, the composer card, the selected chat tab.

paper.usage: Inner paper inside a leaf: capsule bodies and popovers.

paper-2.usage: Tinted paper: code chips, key caps, the slot of a switch, a disabled control.

board.usage: The cardboard face: the rail, the sessions board, and the colour of every button under its paper texture; a rail tile takes its identity colour instead.

board-2.usage: Cardboard's cut edge, 2 to 3px along the bottom and right, and the board's border.

kraft.usage: Kraft paper, always under the paper texture: tabs, labels, notes, tags.

kraft-2.usage: Kraft’s cut edge, and the face of an uncoloured sticker or rail tile (glyphs only in paper: white reads 2.9:1 on it).

mat-green.usage: The sage cardboard mat under a capsule deck, and the sage confirm button. Ground for ink (6.3:1).

mat-green-2.usage: The sage mat's cut edge and border.

mat-red.usage: The terracotta cardboard frame around the composer. Never a text ground.

mat-red-2.usage: The terracotta frame's cut edge, and the face of the destructive button: white reads 6.5:1 on it in paper, 12:1 in night.

mat-red-3.usage: The destructive button's cut edge and border.

ink.usage: Body copy, titles and labels on desk and every paper; the pencil focus ring.

mute.usage: Secondary copy, hand-written counts and durations on sheet, sheet-warm and card (5.3:1 in paper, 6:1 in night).

faint.usage: Placeholders, disabled text and quiet notes. Holds 4.5:1 on paper in both themes.

line.usage: Dashed rules and dividers printed on paper.

rule.usage: The blue-grey ruled lines printed on a note.

bar.usage: Idle effort bars and the outline of an unchecked box.

white.usage: Glyphs and labels printed on a coloured sticker. Never a surface.

sticker-cut.usage: The die-cut border around every sticker, 1.5 to 2px. Always with no shadow. Never on a button.

red.usage: The paw mark, the memory sticker, number badges, the busy pill. White glyphs on it read 4.4:1 in paper and 3.3:1 in night, so keep it to glyphs and bold badges.

red-2.usage: The pull-requests sticker; white reads 7.7:1 on it in paper, 5.8:1 in night.

blue.usage: The sessions sticker. Carries on-blue. The blue button (kr-btn kr-blue, Select).

blue-2.usage: The agents tile and blue’s cut edge.

on-blue.usage: Glyph on a blue sticker: white in paper (6.7:1), ink in night (5.4:1).

green.usage: The MCPs sticker, the idle pill, the Done chip. White glyphs read 3.9:1 in paper: glyphs and hand-written chips only.

amber.usage: The skills and background stickers, the pinwheel's fourth blade, busy durations. White glyphs read 3.5:1 in paper: glyphs only.

max.usage: The workspaces sticker and the MAX stamp.

kind-think.usage: The workflows sticker and thinking kind dots.

kind-sub.usage: The kanban sticker and subagent kind dots.

book.usage: The knowledge base sticker: the book on the rail. White glyphs on it read 6.0:1 in paper and 6.3:1 in night, mixed through dye.

attn.usage: The gold ring around a selected sticker (sticker-on), the attention badge, the needs-you button. Carries on-attn.

highlighter.usage: The raw highlighter colour. Paint with marker, not this.

tape.usage: Tape strips pinning a note to the sheet.

edge.usage: Paper's cut edge: the 1px solid offset under rows, filters, fields and paper buttons.

edge-2.usage: A thicker paper's cut edge, 2px: the chat sheet, the leaf, the composer card.

amb.usage: The cast shadow under cardboard and paper, down and to the right. Never under a sticker.

amb-2.usage: The far, soft shadow under the tallest pieces: boards, the leaf, the composer frame.

face.usage: Top of the face gradient on every cut piece, fading to clear at 55%: the light from the top left.

gloss.usage: Top of the gloss on a sticker, fading to clear at 55%.

marker.usage: Highlighter ink: selected rows, active filters, the on slot of a switch. Always with its strokes and the paper texture.

st-green.usage: Status stickers with white text (Done, Connected). Holds 4.5:1.

st-amber.usage: Status stickers with white text (Running, Connecting). Holds 4.5:1.

st-red.usage: Status stickers and number badges with white text (Failed, Busy). Holds 4.5:1.

deck-1.usage: The steps inside an open capsule.

deck-2.usage: Alternate steps inside an open capsule.

shadow.usage: The edge of a pressed, disabled-looking button.

blush.usage: The soft red wash behind a warning.

stamp-ground.usage: The paper showing inside a rubber stamp.

stamp-ground-soft.usage: A stamp struck over a row.

knob.usage: Outlines drawn over a dark ground.

said.purpose: The agent's narration written in the margin of the sheet.

cover.purpose: The system's name on the cover only.

label.purpose: Buttons, rows, filters, tab names: anything set in a strip of paper or on a sticker.

badge.purpose: Number badges and the busy pill (uppercase, 0.06em tracking).

narrative.overview:
Everything in Primepaw is a piece laid on one cream desk: cardboard that holds things, paper that carries words, stickers that mark things. Nothing is drawn as a box with a border; it is cut out, given a thickness, and set down where it belongs. Depth is height. A board sits on the desk, paper sits on the board, the leaf sits over the tabs, the composer frame sits highest, and a sticker is stuck flat to whichever piece it lives on. The light comes from the top left and never moves, so every piece has one lit face, one cut edge along its bottom and right, and one shadow down and to the right.

The mood is tactile, calm and playful. Tactile: a button is thick card that lifts under the pointer and travels down into the desk when pressed; a row sits down a pixel when clicked; a toggle is a pull-tab sliding in a slot cut into the paper. Calm: nothing pulses, nothing glows, and the only things that keep moving are a working session's pinwheel and the Max effort ring. Playful: the paw, the cat peeking over the composer, rubber stamps, a highlighter that lets the paper show through, and a pinwheel on whatever is busy, each doing a job rather than decorating.

The diorama is explicitly not flat SaaS chrome (one sans for everything, thin grey borders, blur-only shadows, cards nested in cards), not glossy skeuomorphism (glassy bevels, photoreal leather or wood, heavy gradients), and not dark-mode neon (glowing accents, purple-to-blue gradients, cyan on black). Night is the same desk after dark, not a different system.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials, nothing else: cardboard, paper, stickers. Anything that is none of these is printed or written on the paper.
One light, one shadow: a face gradient fading out at 55%, a solid cut edge, one cast shadow in `amb`, always down and to the right.
Depth is stacking, and the stack carries the hierarchy; colour names what a thing is.
Three voices: Caveat written by hand, Fraunces for headings and the agent, Nunito for everything set in type, Courier for code and stamps.
Textures live in the material: paper carries a pulp tile, cardboard a flecked board, and one 40% grain lies over the whole page.
Quick and smooth: 150ms lifts and presses, 260ms landings on a pop ease, loops only while the agent works.

rules.name: The Three Materials Rule
rules.body: Every surface is cardboard, paper or a sticker. Cardboard is never white and never carries body copy; paper carries words; a sticker carries one word or a number, never a sentence, and only the gold `attn` sticker carries words at all.

rules.name: The Own-Edge Rule
rules.body: A piece's cut edge and border are a darker shade of its own colour (`board-2` under `board`, `kraft-2` under `kraft`, `mat-green-2` under `mat-green`). Never cast a cardboard shadow in another colour.

rules.name: The Night Twin Rule
rules.body: Every token has a Night value and nothing is hard-coded. At night boards go dark brown, paper to warm charcoal, the sticker cut to parchment, shadows to black, and identity colours on buttons mix down to 62% into the desk so white glyphs keep 4.5:1.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Nunito 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Caveat 15, 17, 20, 26, 38, 50. Courier 10, 11, 12. Fraunces 15, 17, 20, and 36 for one big figure or initial. Nothing in between.

rules.name: The Written-by-Hand Rule
rules.body: Anything a person would jot (a count, a duration, a placeholder, a show-all link, the word in a switch's slot) is Caveat in ink or faded ink, multiplied into the paper. It is never a badge.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case and verb first ("New session", "Open folder"); hand-written copy is short and lower case ("12 open", "2h ago"); only badges and stamps are uppercase.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the top left and never moves: one lit face, one cut edge on the bottom and right, one shadow down and to the right. A shadow never changes direction.

rules.name: The Flat Sticker Rule
rules.body: A sticker has a die-cut border, gloss across its top and no shadow. It is stuck to one piece and never straddles two.

rules.name: The Depth-Is-Stacking Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is how high a piece sits, not how bright it is. Nothing floats, nothing is blur-only, and no border where a cut edge will do.

rules.name: The Cut-Edge Rule
rules.body: A piece is bounded by its cut edge and the material's own hairline, never by a drawn border or an outline.

rules.name: The Round-Cardboard, Square-Paper Rule
rules.body: 10px on cardboard, 3 to 4px on paper, pills and rounds only on stickers.

dos: Do build every surface as one of three materials: cardboard holds and is pressed, paper carries words, stickers mark things.
Do give every cut piece a face gradient from the top left, a solid cut edge on its bottom and right in a darker shade of its own colour, and one cast shadow in `amb` down and to the right.

Do cut every button, disc and rail tile from thick card with the paper texture over its own colour, 4px corners on buttons, and let it lift 1px on hover and travel 2px right and 3px down when pressed.
Do keep stickers flat: a 2px white die-cut, gloss on top, no shadow, stuck to one piece.
Do carry hierarchy by stacking (desk, board, paper, leaf, frame, sticker) and let colour name what a thing is.
Do use the type scale and nothing in between: Nunito 11 to 15, Caveat 15 to 50, Courier 10 to 12, Fraunces 15, 17, 20 and 36.
Do write counts, durations, placeholders, chips and link buttons by hand in Caveat, ink or faded ink, multiplied into the paper.
Do mark the selected row with real highlighter, the paper showing through, and the selected tab by cutting it from card with a red top edge.
Do use the one sage button for the one committing action on a sheet, the terracotta one for a destructive action, and put a kraft button between them.
Do give every colour a Night value and swap textures to their night tiles; at night mix identity colours on buttons down to 62% so white glyphs hold 4.5:1.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, keep loops to the pinwheel and Max, and keep labels sentence case and verb first.
donts: Don't draw a border where a cut edge will do, and never a blur-only shadow or a shadow in another piece's colour.
Don't let anything float, pulse, glow or bounce; nothing moves unless the agent is working or the user touched it.
Don't put body copy on cardboard, make paper or a sticker pressable, or let a sticker carry a sentence or straddle two pieces.
Don't tilt, scale or rotate cardboard, buttons or paper laid flat; only stickers, stamps and taped or pinned paper lean.
Don't grain a single piece or texture a piece twice: the tile sits in the material and the one page grain lies over everything.
Don't hard-code a colour, paint with the raw highlighter instead of marker, or use a sticker for a live state a stamp or pill already shows.
Don't reach for flat SaaS chrome: no single sans for everything, no thin grey borders, no cards nested in cards.
Don't reach for glossy skeuomorphism: no glassy bevels, no photoreal leather or wood, no heavy gradients beyond the 55% face.
Don't reach for dark-mode neon: no glowing accents, no purple-to-blue gradients, no cyan on black; Night is the same desk after dark.
Don't put more than one sage button on a sheet, place terracotta beside sage, or make a large 40px button anything but a lone call to action.
